findings.problem: After the `change`, the only remaining difference between the two sides is the packet `(Q).physicalPacket t j l u k`, which `referenceFamily_physicalPacket` already identifies with `P.physicalPacket t j (orig j l) u k`. The proof does not rewrite with that equation. Instead it builds a pointwise version `hp` with `congrArg (fun f => f z)`, strips the outer factor with `congr 1`, and passes through an a.e. congruence (`integral_congr_ae` plus `filter_upwards []`) even though the equality holds everywhere. It then rebuilds the entire integrand by hand in a second `congrArg` lambda that repeats the `if |v z-t| ≤ …` expression. The packet term does not depend on the integration variable `z`, so a single rewrite works under the integral binder.
findings.proposed_change:

If the reducible `rfl` that `rw` runs afterwards leaves the goal open, add `rfl`. The original `exact congrArg … (hp z)` shows the sides are definitionally equal after this rewrite.
findings.benefit: The proof then reads as "unfold both coefficients, then replace the restricted family's packet by the original packet", which is the whole mathematical content. The reader no longer has to work through a measure-theoretic detour (a.e. congruence with an empty filter list) or check a second copy of the integrand written inside a lambda.

findings.excerpt:
have hc := congrArg (fun c : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ => c k)
        (P.physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient_eq_zero t a b v g j l u hz)
      dsimp only [f]
      rw [hc]
      simp)
findings.problem: The vanishing side condition only needs this: the frozen coefficient is zero, so the product `coeff k * mask * packet` is zero. The proof first builds the auxiliary equation `hc` by applying `congrArg (fun c => c k)` to the zero lemma, which gives a statement that is not beta-reduced. It then unfolds `f`, rewrites with `hc`, and finishes with a bare `simp`. Since a final `simp` runs anyway, the zero lemma can go straight into it. The first theorem of this file shows that `PiLp.zero_apply` evaluates the zero vector applied to `k`.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the `by` block with
```lean
    (fun l u hz => by
      simp [f, P.physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient_eq_zero t a b v g j l u hz])
```
(or `simp only [f, P.physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient_eq_zero t a b v g j l u hz, PiLp.zero_apply, zero_mul]` if a closed simp set is preferred).
findings.benefit: The side goal then says in one line that the coefficient vanishes and therefore the term vanishes. This matches the parallel vanishing proof in `physicalMainScale_eq_narrow_reference` (line 98), which rewrites with the same zero lemma directly. The reader no longer has to work out what the non-beta-reduced `congrArg` equation `hc` says.
